Sam (dev): running into a weird hang in the Go sample app when resuming a generator stream after a transient 401 -> we refresh token and retry, but the stream goroutine never returns. anyone seen this?
Maria (devex): ugh. do you have a tiny repro? ideally with auth refresh path
Sam (dev): will paste minimal snippet. happens only on longer streams (20-30s), short ones fine. here's the core:
Sam (dev): ```go
ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 45*time.Second)
defer cancel()

c := redwood.NewClient(token)
stream, err := c.Generator.Stream(ctx, req)
if err != nil { return err }

for token := range stream.Tokens() { // blocks forever after auth refresh
   fmt.Print(token.Text)
}
``` 
Tess (eng-ml): hmm, are you reusing the same client/transport after token refresh? If transport roundtripper still holds auth header and we swap token mid-stream it can cause partial handshake mismatch
Sam (dev): we call c.SetToken(newTok) which updates an atomic on the client. other endpoints work fine. only generator.Stream seems to stall.
Maria (devex): can you try forcing a new client after refresh to see if it's the transport state? also what's the server response? any 401s in logs?
Sam (dev): yes there's a 401 followed by successful reissue and retry. client logs show the retry path, but the generator stream goroutine never gets an error or EOF, it just hangs.
Ajay (eng-runtime): tagging in case runtime has seen similar: @Ajay (eng-runtime) any ideas on handshake + auth refresh semantics for generator streaming
Ajay (eng-runtime): I think we have a race where the server accepts a re-auth and issues a new stream id, but the existing client-side stream reader is waiting on a KV cache handshake event that doesn't get replayed after retry. CAUSE: our generator stream handshake expects the initial HTTP/1.1 chunk with 'handshake: ok' and doesn't tolerate mid-stream auth swap
Tess (eng-ml): ok that matches. Workaround: on auth refresh, cancel any in-flight generator contexts so client recreates stream. But we should improve SDK to surface a clear ErrAuthRefresh or similar.
Maria (devex): agree. for DX we should add: (1) doc note in onboarding about token rotation patterns (2) small change: Generator.Stream should return a typed error when underlying transport returns 401 and then retry happened
Sam (dev): workaround helps. curious if we can detect the stuck state from app side — want to avoid aggressive cancels
Ajay (eng-runtime): we can also add a lightweight keepalive ping frame to the stream to gate handshake completion. runtime change needed but smaller than full rebuild
CI Bot: new issue created: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood/issues/4987 - generator-stream-auth-fallback
Maria (devex): thanks @Sam — can you drop a minimal repro gist here? we'll triage and assign
Sam (dev): will do today. also adding this to onboarding checklist so sample app mentions token refresh pattern :thumbsup:
Tess (eng-ml): sounds good. follow-up: add unit test in runtime that simulates mid-stream 401 and verifies stream closes with ErrAuth
Sam (dev): cool, assigning to myself to assemble repro and to test client-new-instance workaround
Maria (devex): closing loop: once repro is posted we'll create a tiny doc blurb for the Go SDK quickstart about "token rotation + streaming generators"
Sam (dev): thanks all :raised_hands:
